svg.title: Crimping the battery's SB50, step by step
svg.desc: Animated, six steps in a 12 second loop, with a numbered step list that lights up in step. This team runs 4 AWG wire in the SB50's 6 AWG contact; the barrel is the tight spot, so every crimp is checked. 1: strip 9/16 in (14 mm) and keep every strand; the cut piece of red insulation slides off. 2: push the wire into the contact's barrel (drawn cut away) so every strand is inside and the insulation butts up to the barrel. 3: crimp in the hex die 25 for 4 AWG; the die must fit the barrel; the dies close. 4: check the crimp: no strands outside the barrel and none trimmed to fit; the barrel closed evenly, not split or flared; the insulation butting up to the barrel. 5: push on the contact, not the insulation, into the housing (drawn cut away) with the notched side of the tongue toward the spring; the spring is pressed down as the tongue passes, then snaps into the notch. 6: tug the wire, then push the contact from the front: a seated contact holds 50 lb. A still panel shows an SB50 from the top: red wire to +, black to -. The housing has no + or - mark, so the wire color is the polarity; wire every SB50 on the team the same way. With reduced motion the drawing shows the checked crimp.
svg.text: Crimping the battery's SB50, step by step
This team's 4 AWG in the 6 AWG contact: the barrel is tight, so check every crimp.

g.text: barrel cut away to show it
Insulation butts up to the barrel
Push on the contact, not the insulation

svg.text: Push the wire into the barrel.
insulation butts up to the barrel
the die must fit the barrel
no strands outside; barrel not split
Push it in until it snaps.
notched side of the tongue to the spring
Tug it, then push it from the front.

g.text: the wire color is the polarity.
Wire every SB50 on the team
